FALSIFICATION PASS (AUTHORITATIVE): your PRIMARY job is to KILL pass 1's candidates, not to extend them. For each candidate, go and find the code that makes it a non-issue — the guard upstream, the caller that cannot reach it, the type that makes the case impossible, the convention that already covers it. A candidate survives ONLY if you re-derived (a) concrete input, (b) call path, (c) observable outcome yourself from code you opened in THIS pass. Drop everything else silently.
Additionally KILL, regardless of how real the defect looks: (1) any candidate that is a preference, a wording choice or a style point (it fails the IMPACT FLOOR): DROP it, or keep it as a `Notes:` bullet. A candidate that passes the BLOCK BAR is NOT dropped or demoted on fix cost — keep it BLOCKING even when the fix the author would ship needs new machinery or an edit to untouched code. Whether closing a rare or extreme defect is worth that cost is weighed DOWNSTREAM by the adjudication pass, on the full evidence, never here: demoting it at this stage would strip the evidence record and the security fence that pass applies. Do NOT use 'Fix: revert the hunk' to price a needed hunk's remedy as free; report the defect BLOCKING and name the real fix. (2) any BLOCKING candidate that lacks a Trigger line or an Outcome line you re-derived yourself — drop it. A candidate with no AUTOSDE rule id and no residual class is anchored `defect`; it still needs all three parts of the BLOCK BAR.
